To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of SEPs in product recovery is a viable option for companies that are willing to invest in the technology.
the proposed multi-criteria decision-making model for the ARTO and DTO systems can be used for optimal decision making in a variety of product recovery scenarios.

the optimal decision for a given set of product recovery problems depends on the following factors: (1) the type and quantity of information available about the products, (2) the type and number of products to be recovered, (3) the type of recovery process to be applied, and (4) the objective function to be optimized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated system that can make optimal product recovery decisions by utilizing the life-cycle information provided by SEPs.
the development of an advanced recovery system, which is based on the concept of sensor-embedded products and is capable of making optimal recovery decisions.
the development of a decision support system for advanced recovery operations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decision making model developed in this study can be used for the optimal design and operation of advanced repair-to-order systems.
the proposed model is a useful tool for the decision making of the advanced repair-to-order (RTO) and disassembly-to order (DTO) systems.
the proposed methodology is able to provide an effective solution for the optimal design of a repair-to-order and/or disassembly-to-order (RDO) system for SEPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an integrated decision support system that can be used to make optimal repair and/or disassembly decisions.
we developed a multi-criteria decision-making model that integrates the life-cycle data from SEPs and the decision-making process for the optimal repair and disassembly decisions.
we have developed a novel decision making model for a repair-to-order and a disassembly-to-order systems that can take into account the information provided by the embedded sensor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of SEPs can reduce the uncertainty involved in product recovery and increase the recovery rate.
SEPs can be recovered more effectively than conventional products.

, by incorporating the remaining useful life information into the recovery decision making process, it is possible not only to improve the performance of the recovery system but also to reduce the complexity of the recovery process by eliminating the need for inspection and disassembly operations.
